newsitem.title: USA: Tandycrafts sees restructuring pay in FY98.
newsitem.headline: Tandycrafts sees restructuring pay in FY98.

text.p: Tandycrafts Inc, reporting a $1.9 million net loss for the fiscal year ended June 30, said Tuesday it would see restructuring benefits in its 1998 fiscal year and beyond.

"While the results for fiscal 1997 reflect the costs of (restructuring), the benefits of those decisions will be realized beginning in fiscal 1998 and beyond," said chief executive Michael Walsh in a statement.
Tandycrafts Tuesday posted a $1.9 million net loss, or $0.15 per share, for the fiscal year ended June 30, compared with a $10.7 million net loss, or $0.89 per share, in fiscal 1996.

The specialty retailer and manufacturer said the 1997 results include pretax charges of $5.3 million to reposition its Joshua's Christian Stores chain. It added it took pretax restructuring charges of $18.3 million in fiscal 1996.

The company earned $701,000, or $0.06 per share, in the fourth quarter, compared with $1.3 million, or $0.11 per share, in the 1996 quarter. Sales in the quarter dropped to $59.5 million from $64.0 million last year. Excluding discontinued operations, sales increased 2.9 percent, or $l.7 million, over last year's quarter, Tandycrafts added.

"Fiscal 1997 was a transition year which continued the strategic rebuilding and repositioning of the company's operations which started with the restructuring plan initiated in fiscal 1996," Walsh said.

The chief executive added the restructuring already paid off at its Joshua's chain, which posted same-store sales gains of 8.6 percent and a "significant improvement in operating income" in the quarter ended June 30.
The company's stock closed at 4-11/16 Monday.
